title: Dirac Labs Raises $1.8M Pre-Seed Round to Scale Diamond-Based Quantum Navigation Sensors - Quantum Computing Report
gist: University of Wisconsin-Madison spinout Dirac Labs raised a $1.8M pre-seed round led by Microsoft/Green Bay Packers venture TitletownTech to commercialize a diamond NV-center magnetometry sensor that delivers GPS-independent, jam-proof positioning for defense, maritime, and industrial customers.

insights.claim: University of Wisconsin-Madison spinout Dirac Labs Inc. raised $1.8 million USD in pre-seed funding led by TitletownTech (a joint venture of Microsoft and the Green Bay Packers), with participation from Automotive Ventures, Riceberg Ventures, quantumEDGE Ventures, gradCapital, and angel investors Balaji Srinivasan and Jude Gomila.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The notable mix of corporate VC and prominent tech angels signals early cross-sector interest (defense-tech, mobility) in diamond-based quantum sensing, a nascent sub-sector worth tracking for follow-on rounds.
insights.locator: University of Wisconsin-Madison spinout Dirac Labs

insights.claim: Dirac Labs has also secured non-dilutive public grant funding from NOAA (via gener8tor), the Indo-U.S. Science and Technology Forum, the Mercatus Center at George Mason University, and the Wisconsin Entrepreneurship Hub.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Diversified public grant support reduces near-term dilution risk and signals government validation of the technology's national-security relevance.
insights.locator: the company has also secured non-dilutive public grant funding

insights.claim: Dirac Labs' NVD-4 sensor uses diamond NV-center magnetometry to passively measure local variations in Earth's geomagnetic field, providing GPS-independent positioning that works underwater, underground, and in radio-frequency jammed or spoofed environments.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Addresses a structural defense and maritime pain point (GPS denial) with a passive, hard-to-jam sensing approach, a differentiated moat versus classical inertial navigation.

insights.claim: Real-time AI models handle Dirac Labs' signal processing and sensor fusion, converting faint geomagnetic inputs into precise location fixes while compensating for environmental noise and platform vibration.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Highlights the AI-quantum sensing convergence theme; value capture may depend as much on the software fusion layer as on the underlying quantum hardware.

insights.claim: The golf-ball sized NVD-4 sensor is designed as a plug-and-play unit that connects directly into standard GPS device ports on aircraft, submarines, autonomous underwater vehicles, and industrial mining equipment, and is manufactured using standard CMOS semiconductor foundry processes.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A drop-in form factor plus CMOS-compatible manufacturing lowers integration friction and cost, improving the odds of rapid adoption across defense and industrial customers versus bespoke hardware.
